question: Without fitting amplitude or density response, does P4D's fixed marked-Poisson implication RMS proportional to sqrt(developed density) reproduce the normalized shape and high-density behavior of the extracted NASA Tables 4-6 series?

evaluation.normalization: divide observed RMS and sqrt-density prediction by their values at the lowest-density row of each table/aperture series
evaluation.rank_metric: Spearman correlation over every eligible full-density series
evaluation.turnover_metric: whether the observed maximum occurs at the highest-density row, as required by unchanged monotone P4D

allowed_after_pass: retain P4D's monotone density-amplitude shape as one generic measured-compatible control
seek independent non-radiographic confirmation before any photographic use
forbidden: fit a scale, exponent, peak density or aperture response
drop individual tables, apertures or high-density rows
reinterpret radiographic film as consumer colour-film stock evidence
attribute deviations to processing chemistry as supervision truth

branch_rule.pass: Retain only a generic normalized density/granularity shape control; no calibration claim.
branch_rule.fail: Close P4D measured-shape compatibility without retuning. A separately frozen peaked-density exploratory primitive may be studied, but this source cannot provide confirmatory stock evidence.

claim_ceiling: No-fit normalized shape comparison between one generic marked-Poisson primitive and nine series from one historical radiographic-film report; not amplitude calibration, modern camera-film evidence, stock response or product validation.
